decisions.basis: The interval dimension is explicit, but the target organ is left generic and appears reconstructed from a single-organ repeat order rather than clearly identified in the visible question state.
The question and typed requirement explicitly ask for change in appendiceal, bowel, fluid, or uterine findings relative to prior CT/radiograph.
The repeated CT question explicitly asks whether established appendicitis progressed or developed interval complications.
The requirement explicitly compares pancreatic inflammation, collections, ascites, and hepatobiliary findings with prior CT and ultrasound.
The requirement explicitly asks whether hepatobiliary abnormalities are new, progressive, or unchanged relative to prior imaging.
The biliary question requires comparison with prior ultrasound for improvement, stability, or progression.
The typed requirement explicitly asks for interval change in duct dilation and gallbladder distention.
The repeat ultrasound asks for change in duct dilation and pericholecystic fluid relative to immediately preceding imaging.
The question explicitly asks whether pancreatitis and local complications progressed relative to the preceding CT.
The serial CT question explicitly requires progression, stability, or improvement relative to the most recent CT.
The serial CT question requires interval assessment of necrosis, inflammation, and new or enlarging collections.
The question and requirement explicitly ask whether pancreatitis-related collections and abdominal findings have progressed.
The question explicitly asks about progression of necrotizing pancreatitis and interval change in necrosis, ascites, and collections.
The question explicitly asks for progression of necrosis, collections, compartment physiology, and bowel pathology relative to prior imaging.
CT recharacterizes and extends an incompletely characterized ultrasound lesion; the findings are not irreconcilable evidence streams about the same proposition.
The prior diagnostic CT already covered the repeated broad structural question; the record requires review for an undocumented new-time-point or management trigger.
The prior ultrasound already covered the same hepatobiliary requirements; institutional confirmation or a new-time-point need may exist but is not represented in the current question.

The question explicitly asks for progression and new complications, while requirement reasons admit prior studies cannot answer interval change; the missing temporal requirement makes sufficiently_answered internally inconsistent.
